Nolan Kido / A practical AI method

AI Works, Human Decides

Give AI a defined job. Keep authority and accountability with the people affected. I use three rules:

  • AI Works. Set the permitted inputs, output and stopping point before delegating a draft, organization task or code change.
  • Human Decides. People choose the purpose, review facts and consequences, authorize commitments, and can reject the result.
  • Proof Matters. Check claims independently. Count setup, review, corrections and maintenance when deciding whether AI helped.

Read Let AI do more. Keep the judgment for the reasoning behind this approach and two recorded examples.

Follow the four checkpoints: Decide, Brief, Check, Measure. The browser tools make no AI calls.

Verification and impact require different evidence. The October 11 website-repair case shows how a malformed closing tag escaped 347 passing tests until an HTML5 parser caught it. The separate website-visibility case documents later release checks and a free Search Console method while keeping search outcomes unmeasured. Neither establishes higher rankings.

This working standard cannot replace professional review when consequences are high. About Nolan Kido.

One task / Four useful checkpoints

Decide. Brief. Check. Measure.

Start with one task you want to make easier. Use the stages you need, then decide whether the result is worth keeping. A simpler method or a decision to stop is a valid endpoint.

  1. 01 / Decide

    Decide whether AI fits the task

    Check the purpose, permitted inputs, consequences and a simpler alternative before starting.

    What you keep: A decision to pause, use a simpler method, prepare first or try a bounded draft.

  2. 02 / Brief

    Write a brief with a finish line

    Name the useful result, supplied material, boundaries and checks before delegating production.

    What you keep: A written brief that keeps assumptions, permissions and responsibilities visible.

  3. 03 / Check

    Check the answer against evidence

    Choose checks for facts, numbers, summaries, writing, code or advice. Follow the source-review example when the task is a summary.

    What you keep: An evidence record for the consequential claims, with untested parts still visible.

  4. 04 / Measure

    Compare the whole cost of the task

    Count preparation, production, review, repairs, setup and upkeep at the same acceptable quality.

    What you keep: A time comparison and a choice to keep, adjust, stop or gather more observations.

These are thinking aids and browser tools. No AI runs here, and following the path does not certify accuracy, safety or time savings. For a summary, inspect the source-to-summary worked example; other answers need checks suited to their use.

AI ANSWER REVIEW RECORD
Nolan Kido
Guide: https://nolankido.com/technology/check-ai-answers/

Keep this copy privately in your own notes. Do not put private answers in a
public repository. This is a thinking aid, not an automatic accuracy test.

1. NAME THE USE
What would I do with this answer?
Which parts could change an action, commitment, amount, or conclusion?
What would happen if those parts were wrong?

2. CHOOSE THE RELEVANT CHECKS
An answer can need several checks.
- Facts/citations: locate the real source, supporting passage, scope and date.
- Numbers: verify inputs and units; recompute the full calculation separately.
- Summary: preserve the source's meaning, conditions, uncertainty and ownership.
- Writing: verify facts, voice, requests and promises; separate draft from send.
- Code/website: test distinguishing cases and failures; check the released version.
- Personal advice: separate verified facts, predictions and assumed priorities.

3. RECORD ONE IMPORTANT CLAIM AT A TIME
Exact claim or behavior:
Evidence outside the AI answer (source/passages, original material or test):
Date/version/context of that evidence:
Independent check actually performed:
Observed result:
Evidence status (supported for the stated purpose / contradicted / unresolved):
Why the evidence supports that status:
Remaining unknowns or limits:
Change needed:

Repeat section 3 for each consequential claim. A second AI agreeing is not
independent evidence that the claim is true.
Use unresolved when evidence is missing or insufficient to decide whether
the claim is supported or contradicted for the stated purpose.
Missing support alone is not contradictory evidence.

4. DECIDE THE NEXT STEP
Named part and purpose I am prepared to use:
Parts to revise, leave unused or investigate further:
Who needs to review or approve any consequential decision or external action?
What would make me revisit this result?

A check supports only the claim, inputs, scope and version it actually tested.
A faithful summary can preserve an inaccurate source. Correct arithmetic can
use incorrect inputs. A reviewed draft is not permission to send or publish.

================================================================
4. MEASURE
Guide: https://nolankido.com/technology/ai-time-savings/
Original blank worksheet: https://nolankido.com/downloads/workflow-time-review.txt
================================================================

WORKFLOW TIME REVIEW
Use privately. Do not include confidential task material.

Task and acceptance standard:
Comparison window and repetition count (N):
Basis: planning estimates / observed times (describe how collected)
Usual effort per task (M), minutes:
Assisted preparation and production per task (A), minutes:
Review and repair per assisted task (R), minutes:
One-time setup (S), minutes:
Upkeep across the comparison window (K), minutes:

Compare the same work at the same acceptable quality. Use a consistent
measure of effort. Count waiting only when it prevents other useful work;
do not count a minute twice. Include failed attempts and cleanup.

Usual total = N * M
Assisted total = S + K + N * (A + R)
Net time saved = N * (M - A - R) - S - K

If M - A - R is positive, no net time loss begins at the ceiling of
(S + K) / (M - A - R), with at least one repetition.
Strictly positive savings begin at floor((S + K) / (M - A - R)) + 1.
These thresholds hold setup and upkeep fixed. Recalculate if they grow.
If the per-task difference is zero or negative, repeating the workflow
does not create positive time savings at those costs.

Quality check: not yet checked / met / not met
What was checked, against which source or independent example?
What failed or needed repair?
Privacy, money, reliability, enjoyment, and effects on other people:
Uncertainty and what would change the decision:
Decision: keep / adjust / stop / gather more observations
Next review point:

An estimate is not a measured outcome. A before/after observation alone
is not proof that AI caused the change. This is a time comparison, not
financial ROI, a safety assessment, or a quality score.

Nolan Kido | https://nolankido.com/technology/ai-time-savings/

FINAL TASK DECISION
What I will actually use:
What remains unverified or needs another person:
Keep / adjust / stop / gather more observations:
Reason and next review point:

A faithful summary can preserve an inaccurate source. Correct arithmetic
can use wrong inputs. A reviewed draft is not permission to send or
publish. Estimates are not observed results, and a before/after change
alone does not show that AI caused it. Keep those limits with the record.

Small business / One accountable pilot

How can a small business start using AI on a real workflow?

Choose one repeatable, reversible task that produces a reviewable draft, such as a customer reply or a summary of approved public notes. Keep sending, promises, financial decisions, private records and customer-account changes outside this first pilot.

  1. Decide. Name the result, simpler alternative and permitted inputs. Pause if permissions are unclear. Use the task-choice guide.
  2. Brief. Specify required facts, prohibited claims, format, reviewer and stop condition. Build a task brief before trying a model.
  3. Establish a baseline. Record the manual process at acceptable quality. Use fictional, public or explicitly approved examples. Keep inputs, prompts, outputs, corrections and rejected drafts together privately.
  4. Check. Compare facts and promises with authorized sources. Try a missing complaint and an invented offer. Require a person's approval. Inspect the offline reply audit for a limited example.
  5. Measure. Count preparation, model use, review, corrections, setup, maintenance and failed attempts at the same acceptable quality. Keep the manual fallback. Use the full-workflow time calculator with observations or labeled estimates.

A concrete approval boundary: a fictional review reply

A fictional customer reports a duplicate charge and an unanswered question. AI may draft an acknowledgment of both. It may not invent a refund policy, promise compensation, retrieve private records or send the reply. A person checks the facts, authorizes any promise and decides whether to publish.

The Review Reply Writer case and separate evidence audit demonstrate that boundary using historical fictional examples. They do not establish client deployment, savings, compliance or a general model reliability rate.

When to stop: unauthorized input, an unsupported promise, a failed acceptance check, or total effort that does not justify the result. For broader risk-management background, see the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. This educational pilot outline is not a NIST assessment or a substitute for legal, security or professional review.

Recorded AI-assisted work / Identity evidence

How an AI-assisted audit corrected a public identity claim.

On November 4, 2026, an AI-assisted review found role and credential claims in this site's public JSON-LD identity file that the reviewed evidence did not support. The visible About page did not make those claims. Pull request #180 removed them while preserving the Person identifier, scholarly article and existing profile links.

The revised source and published JSON-LD matched on readback. That verifies the correction, not search-engine use, better rankings, AI citations or visitor trust.

Reading this table: On a narrow screen, swipe sideways within the table to see all columns. With a keyboard, focus the table and use the left or right arrow key.

What the public repository records before and after the correction
Claim or dataBeforePublished decision
Startup and investingjobTitle asserted “AI Startup Founder and Angel Investor.”Removed a title without sufficient public corroboration in the reviewed record. This does not assert the title was never true.
Academic credentialshasCredential and alumniOf listed two University of Hawaiʻi degrees.Removed pending a documented credential review. An absence of reviewed evidence does not mean a degree was not earned.
MIT research roleaffiliation described “Research Affiliate.”Removed. An MIT-hosted manuscript supports a publication record, not employment or an appointment.
Authorship and stable identityA shared Person ID, external profiles and a 2012 scholarly article.Kept the original author identifier, existing profile links and peer-reviewed accounting article. The description now leads with bounded practical-AI work.

How the work was checked

  1. Read the records. Compare the public before file and after file.
  2. Separate support from inference. Coauthorship does not establish an institutional appointment; public code does not establish a business outcome.
  3. Limit the edit. Remove unsupported claims and retain documented work, identifiers and citations. The separate historical COO description remained historical.
  4. Verify publication. Parse and compare source and published data, then inspect the committed diff. This checks the change, not every remaining biographical claim.

Reproduce the bounded comparison

Download the two complete public JSON-LD files linked above as before.jsonld and after.jsonld. Save the offline Python identity-evidence gate in the same folder. With Python 3.10+ on Windows:

py -3 identity-evidence-gate.py --self-test
py -3 identity-evidence-gate.py --before before.jsonld --after after.jsonld

Five synthetic self-tests check expected pass and fail scenarios. The comparison checks structural invariants, not biography: exit code 0 means those checks passed, 2 reports findings, and 1 reports an input or execution error. It runs offline without an account or AI request. Download the case record and reusable evidence worksheet.

What remains a human decision

I authorized the improvement process; the assistant made the scoped edit. This was not independent human verification of every credential, employer or account-ownership claim. Restoring a title or degree requires a suitable source, precise dates and a disclosure decision. My About page links the available evidence.

The lesson: keep an evidence trail and a correction path. A structural checker is not a truth checker. This single-site case does not measure AI editing quality or business returns.

AI in real life / Evidence changes with the task

AI judgment in software, small-business workflows, and poker

I ask what evidence would justify using an answer. The checks depend on the task:

  • Software: A website repair that passed 347 tests still had an HTML defect. Test results are evidence within their scope, not proof that every browser experience works.
  • Small-business AI: The review-reply evidence audit uses archived example drafts and deliberate counterexamples to demonstrate a checking process. Its offline controls do not establish a real-world business error rate.
  • Tournament poker: A recorded Portland Meadows hand separates known action from retrospective interpretation. A hand's outcome does not by itself validate a decision or substitute for a complete solver analysis.

Explore my poker hand-review method and the essays AI Works, Human Decides and When to Trust the AI vs. When to Trust Human Instinct. The essays explain my perspective, rather than independently verifying project outcomes.

Creative production / A human evidence gate

How I check an AI-assisted poker vlog edit against the hand record.

AI can draft a story or overlay, but it cannot establish missing cards or turn hindsight into a thought I had at the table. The Portland Meadows Episode 1 companion supplies two hands for this proposed release standard. This proposed standard does not establish that earlier uploads passed it.

Read the full AI-and-poker editing case for proposed captions, arithmetic and an offline check. The captions are examples, not graphics verified in the released video.

Reading this table: On a narrow screen, swipe sideways within the table to see all columns. With a keyboard, focus the table and use the left or right arrow key.

What a graphics and narration review can use from the published companion
MomentSource-supported factsDo not silently fill in
6-4 offsuit near the money bubbleSmall blind, 13 players left with 10 paid, about 148,000 chips at a 15,000 big blind, approximately 9.87 BB; shove called by A-K suitedIndividual hole-card suits, complete board, exact effective stack or a numerical solver endorsement
Pocket sevens four-handedBig blind, about 585,000 chips at a 30,000 big blind, 19.5 BB; button's 75,000 open is 2.5 BB; reshove called by A-T offsuit, sevens holdFull runout, opponent's full opening range, unobserved thoughts or a verified ICM conclusion
Tournament result graphicAdvertised first prize was $5,100; my reported payment after the four-way deal was $2,900Confusing advertised first prize with received payout, or describing either amount as net profit
  1. Lock the source. Record facts, evidence links and unknowns for each hand. Separate footage notes from later recollections.
  2. Match narration and graphics. Check positions, stacks, bets, pot arithmetic, cards and outcomes. Omit unknown suits or label them as illustrative.
  3. Label hindsight. Retrospective analysis is not an in-the-moment calculation or a verified solver result.
  4. Review the release cut. Old version 7 chapter offsets remain unverified for the current upload.
  5. Require human approval. Accept, revise or hold each scene. Check music, footage, venue rules and privacy separately.

Download the truth-to-screen QA worksheet (.md) for examples and a blank scene review. Use it privately without an account or model request.

This proposed control does not establish better retention, verified strategy, edit speed, filming permission or unpublished footage quality. The creator workbench covers the broader story and graphics workflow.

Worked example / Offline QA

Seven constructed edit conflicts. Seven targeted flags.

To make the truth-to-screen release gate testable, I wrote a small standard-library Python checker for structured edit claims from the public Portland Meadows Episode 1 record. This is a deterministic audit of text fields, not an AI watching my footage. I constructed four fictional, incorrect scene records and paired each with a corrected record. The checker found the seven expected targeted conflicts in the constructed records and none in the corrected examples.

Reading this table: On a narrow screen, swipe sideways within the table to see all columns. With a keyboard, focus the table and use the left or right arrow key.

Reproducible demonstrations, not observed defects in a released video
Constructed before editTargeted flagsCorrected after edit
Unverified suits and complete board shown as factual2: suits, boardOmit the unverified details: 0
Pocket sevens shown at 18 BB with a 2 BB button open2: stack, raise-to amount19.5 BB and 2.5 BB from the reported chips: 0
Advertised $5,100 shown as the amount received1: payout conflictReport $2,900 after the four-way deal: 0
A verified solver verdict and old version 7 chapter offset are claimed2: unsupported solver, unverified chapter timingRemove both unsupported assertions: 0

Download the standalone Python checker (.py). Its built-in --self-test reproduces the four comparisons and confirms the expected seven-to-zero flag counts. --example prints a local JSON starter record, and --check SCENES.json checks only supplied structured scene fields. The worksheet contains the commands and the final human review checklist. No model, account, uploaded video, internet connection or paid API is required.

What this does not establish: The four before cases are deliberately written test fixtures, not flaws observed in an actual edit or model-generated mistakes. A clean structured result does not confirm that spoken audio matches graphics, establish missing suits, verify solver strategy, secure filming rights or predict viewer retention. The checker's sources are bounded to those three public Episode 1 fact records; other hands require separate human verification.
